description: The usage a Codex CLI 0.160.1 exec --json stream reports on turn.completed is the thread's cumulative token usage as of that turn's completion (ThreadTokenUsage.total): a cumulative snapshot at session scope, not a per-turn measurement. The running total adds a response's usage only when that response's completion carried one (ResponseEvent::Completed.token_usage is an Option; TokenUsageInfo::append_last_usage), and the deserializer writes 0 for an omitted cache-write, cached or reasoning member. In canonical tranches (0.8.0-prototype): cache reads 52352 and output 164 are copied as Lower bounds (the thread's actual quantities are at least these values and may exceed them; a positive running total does not establish that every response reported); the cache-write 0 and reasoning 0 are Possibly default; output 164 includes the reasoning tokens. input_tokens 63434 includes the 52352 cached tokens (TokenUsage::non_cached_input), so 63434 - 52352 = 11082 is the uncached input only if the cache-write 0 was measured and both operands are complete: it is the uncached component's conditional value (Conditional), and the canonical uncached tranche stays absent (Unavailable). Authored from the pinned emitter, protocol and API client, independently of the writer's mapper and the oracle's profile; the numbers are the live recording's own.

counterexamples.why: Turn completion is when the emitter writes the thread's cumulative total; it is not evidence that the measurement covers only this turn. The components are equal under both readings; the scope is the meaning.
Codex input_tokens includes the cached tokens; copying it as the uncached tranche would price 52352 cache reads twice, once at the input rate.
A running total of the thread is not the consumption of one unit; two snapshots overlap and are never summed.
reasoning_output_tokens is the Responses API breakdown of output_tokens; stating it separate would invite adding it to output.
The pinned deserializer writes cache_write_tokens 0 when the provider omits it, so a reported 0 is not a measured zero even inside non-zero usage.
The difference uses the possibly defaulted cache-write 0 and two running totals that may omit responses; it is not an established measurement of the uncached input.

A formula result that holds only under the named assumptions is the component's conditional value, never the canonical uncached tranche: a consumer summing uncached_input_tokens would otherwise mix an exact quantity with an assumption.

The thread running total adds only the responses whose completion carried usage and writes 0 for an omitted member, so a positive total does not establish that every response's contribution was reported; it is at least this value, not a measurement of the whole.
